paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is about: Jesus can be trusted with what you don't have. The crowd had nothing to eat, and the disciples asked, "Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?" (Mark 8:4). Jesus had compassion on that crowd (Mark 8:2), and He still does on His people. When your dough bowl is EMPTY, He is not nervous about it.

Now look at the boat. The disciples had one loaf and a whole lot of worry, and Jesus asked them, "Do you still not see or understand?" (Mark 8:17). They had just collected seven basketfuls of leftovers (Mark 8:8), and I think they were still counting crumbs instead of remembering. Jesus didn't ask them to be strong. He asked, "And do you not remember?" (Mark 8:18).

So here's the takeaway, baker. Remembering what Jesus has already done is how you stop panicking over what you don't have yet. The Pharisees demanded a sign right after a meal that was a sign (Mark 8:11-12). Don't be like me checking the cooling rack every thirty seconds, and trust the One who already filled the baskets.
